title: Per-trial data row — WM × Imagery follow-up experiment
description: JSON Schema for one row of jsPsych data emitted during a session. Every row carries a `phase` discriminator; per-phase fields are documented as optional in this top-level schema and constrained by the `oneOf` per-phase variants in `$defs`. Engineering non-negotiable #6 in design/Coding_Agent_Prompt.md: every row written by the runner validates against this document.

phase.description: The phase discriminator. Locked taxonomy below — analysis scripts filter on this field. Adding a new phase requires updating both this enum and the runtime emitter that writes it.

trial_type.description: jsPsych built-in: the plugin name that produced this row (e.g. 'html-keyboard-response', 'survey-html-form'). It is NOT the experimental condition; use `condition`.

trial_index.description: jsPsych built-in: zero-based index of the row across the entire session.

time_elapsed.description: ms since the experiment started. jsPsych sets it on trial rows; rows written outside a trial (star rows, events) get the value at the time of writing, or null before the timeline started.

internal_node_id.description: jsPsych built-in: dotted-path locator of the timeline node that produced this row.

rt.description: jsPsych built-in: response time in ms (null if no response was given).

response.description: jsPsych built-in: the response payload. String for keyboard plugins, object for survey plugins. Null when no response.

seq.description: Auto-incrementing sequence number stamped by the IndexedDB storage layer (`storage.js`). Used by the chunked uploader to advance the upload cursor.

trial_index_in_block.description: RAW value, 0-based: index of the trial in its condition's 24-trial pool (0-23; exported 1-24 as `pool_index` and in the wide files' `Trial`). It is NOT the order of presentation and it repeats across conditions and across main_a / main_b; identify a trial with `trial_uid`, order trials with `presentation_index`. On `pattern_phase` rows the value is the presentation position in the block of the trial that follows.

rotation_deg.description: Rotation of the grid and pattern for the trial, an integer in -90..90 (clockwise positive; 0 and both end points allowed). Drawn from six strata (-90..-61, -60..-31, -30..-1, 0..30, 31..60, 61..90), 4 per stratum in each 24-trial condition, 12 negative and 12 non-negative. Absent for d_only (which records display_rotation_deg instead) and t_only.

display_rotation_deg.description: Rotation at which the grid is shown in a d_only trial, an integer in -90..90 (clockwise positive; 0 allowed), drawn by the same sampler from the same six strata as `rotation_deg`, and reached through the same rotation animation (500 ms) and stabilisation (1000 ms) as the imagery trials. Present on d_only rows only.

probe_position.description: RAW value, 0-based: order of this recognition test (or of this star) within the trial's 3 tests (0-2; exported 1-3 as `probe_position` / `test_position`).

encoding_position.description: RAW value, 0-based (0-2; exported 1-3): encoding position, among the three memory items of one kind, tied to the probe by the scheduler. For a target probe it is the position of the item that was probed. For a foil it is a label only (no item was encoded for it). Present on probe rows of all four memory conditions.

probe_type.description: Four-probe-type taxonomy from design §6.2: T = target (was-encoded), F = foil (never-encoded); on/off = on- vs off-pattern cell.

probed_cell.description: Cell index on the 5×5 grid (0–24) where the probe appeared.

probe_pattern_label.description: Whether the probed cell is on the 13-cell gray pattern (minus centre) or off it.

probed_tone_index.description: Index into the 24-tone bank for the probed tone (T-only / I+T only).

probed_tone_freq_hz.description: Frequency of the probed tone in Hz (log-equally spaced between config.tones.low_freq_hz and config.tones.high_freq_hz).

is_target.description: True iff the probe is a target (was encoded), false for foils.

responded.description: True iff the participant pressed a valid response key within the response window.

said_yes.description: Yes/no response on memory-probe rows. Null if no response (timeout / wrong key).

said_on.description: On/off response on imagery-star rows (i.e., did the participant judge the star to be on the pattern?). Null if no response.

response_key.description: Raw key pressed (e.g., 'arrowright', 'j'). Null if no response.

response_rt_ms.description: Response time in ms of the FIRST valid key press relative to the onset stamp of the same stimulus (star: `star_onset_ts_ms`; recognition probe: `probe_onset_ts_ms`, written in `rt`), from the key event timestamp, rounded, at least 1. Null if no response (then `responded` is false). `response_ts_ms` is the timestamp of that key press, so the value can be re-derived as `response_ts_ms - <onset stamp>` (+-1 ms rounding).

response_ts_ms.description: performance.now() timestamp (rounded ms) of the first valid key press (the key event's own timestamp), on the same scale as `probe_onset_ts_ms` / `star_onset_ts_ms`. Stamped on every recognition-probe row (`*_probe`) and star row (`*_star`); null if the stimulus was not answered. Re-derive the response time as `response_ts_ms - probe_onset_ts_ms` (or `- star_onset_ts_ms`), +-1 ms rounding.

probe_correct.description: Whether the participant's yes/no probe response was correct (true) or incorrect / non-response (false). Memory-probe rows.

star_correct.description: Whether the participant's star response (on/off judgement) was correct. Imagery-star rows.

slot_index_in_seq.description: RAW value, 0-based: slot within the trial's 6-slot M/S sequence (0-5; exported 1-6 as `slot_in_stream`).

pattern_label.description: Whether a star or dot occupied an on-pattern or off-pattern cell.

attention_check_id.description: Identifier for the typed-instruction attention check (design §11.4).

attention_check_raw.description: Raw participant typed input (un-normalised) for the attention check.

attention_check_passed.description: True iff `normalise(raw) === normalise(expected_answer)` (trim + lowercase, no punctuation strip).

attention_total.description: Distinct attention checks administered, stamped on the `attention_check_summary` row.

attention_passed.description: Distinct attention checks passed the first time they were shown.

attention_failed.description: Distinct attention checks failed the first time they were shown (the count the exclusion rule uses).

attention_failed_final.description: Distinct attention checks failed on their final administration (differs from `attention_failed` only after a practice re-loop).

attention_administrations.description: Attention-check rows administered in total; above `attention_total` when the practice loop repeated the checks.

exit_reason.description: Why the session ended early. Present only on the exit row (`desktop_gate_fail`, `consent_declined`, `tone_audibility_fail`, `screen_calibration_fail`, `timing_probe_fail`, `practice_disqualification`, `inter_block_rest_timeout`).

strategy_section.description: Section identifier for the strategy questionnaire row, matching the trailing portion of the row's `phase` (e.g. `strategy_i_d` → `i_d`).

strategy_responses.description: Map from strategy item id (`strategy_q01`..`strategy_q19`) to the participant's selected option value (a string in {'1','2','3','4','5'} on the 5-point agreement Likert; 1 = Strongly disagree, 5 = Strongly agree) or null if blank. Each of the five strategy_* rows carries only the items belonging to its section; the analyst collapses them via `scoreStrategy` (src/questionnaire/strategy.js).

music_experience_responses.description: Map from music-experience item id (me_q01–me_q08) to the participant's selected option value (string code, e.g. '4-5', '1.5', 'intermediate', 'yes') or null if blank. Items me_q01..me_q07 are the seven items of the Goldsmiths Musical Sophistication Index v1.0 Musical Training subscale in the order of File S1 of Müllensiefen, Gingras, Musil & Stewart (2014, *PLOS ONE* 9(2) e89642), each scored 1..7; me_q03 ('I have never been complimented for my talents as a musical performer') and me_q07 ('I would not consider myself a musician') are negatively phrased and reverse-scored (raw 1 scores 7, raw 7 scores 1) — the stored value is the raw option, the reversal is applied in scoring; the composite is the sum, range 7..49 (analyst computes via `goldMsiMtComposite`). Item me_q08 is a self-reported absolute-pitch flag, kept outside the composite. Categorical covariate fields used for sensitivity analysis after the §3.2 non-musical tone-bank redesign (draft revisions 2026-05-05 and 2026-05-07).

consented.description: True iff the participant clicked the 'I consent' button on the consent screen.

cc_px_width.description: Credit-card calibration width in CSS pixels at the moment the participant clicked 'this matches my card'.

px_per_mm.description: Derived px/mm conversion for the participant's display, stamped on the screen-calibration row.

tones_audible.description: Stamped on `tone_audibility_and_comfort` rows. True iff the participant clicked 'I'm comfortable — continue' before the 10-sweep cap was hit; false iff the sweep cycled through the bank ten times without a press, which routes to the `tone_audibility_fail` exit.

user_playback_pct.description: Final position of the in-page playback-volume slider (0..100) at the moment the participant pressed Yes (or at the moment the 10-sweep timeout fired). Stamped on `tone_audibility_and_comfort` rows.

user_playback_gain.description: Linear scalar (`user_playback_pct / 100`) applied to every subsequent tone the experiment plays via `playSineTone` / `playPinkNoise`. Stamped on `tone_audibility_and_comfort` rows.

sweeps_completed.description: Number of full 24-tone sweeps that started before the participant pressed Yes (or before the 10-sweep cap halted the loop). Stamped on `tone_audibility_and_comfort` rows.

completion_redirect_url.description: URL the participant was redirected to at session end (or null if the placeholder URL skipped redirect).

completion_was_placeholder.description: True iff the configured completion URL still contained the `PLACEHOLDER` token at session end (test-build flag).

arrow_cue_onset_ts_ms.description: performance.now() timestamp (rounded to whole ms, since document time origin) at which the rotation-arrow cue became visible. Stamped on `i_only_arrow_cue` / `i_d_arrow_cue` / `i_t_arrow_cue` rows. Use with `trial_start_gate_onset_ts_ms` to recover the cue→gate latency exactly; use with `gate_passed_at_ms` (relative to gate onset) to derive a session-stable pre-imagine duration.

trial_start_gate_onset_ts_ms.description: performance.now() timestamp (rounded ms) when the trial-start gate rendered (the empty-circle frame the participant looks at while pre-imagining the rotated pattern and pressing both arrow keys). Stamped on `*_trial_start` rows. Combine with `gate_passed_at_ms` (relative offset already on the row) to compute the absolute moment the participant armed the trial.

encoding_onset_ts_ms.description: performance.now() timestamp (rounded ms) at which the encoding node's grid frame mounted (i.e. when the on_load hook fired). Stamped on `d_only_encoding`, `t_only_encoding`, `i_only_encoding`, `i_d_encoding`, `i_t_encoding` rows. For imagery conditions, the first encoded slot starts ROTATION_ANIMATION_MS + POST_ROTATION_MS later than this timestamp; for D-only / T-only the first slot starts immediately.

slot_onsets_ts_ms.description: Per-slot performance.now() timestamps (rounded ms) captured at the moment each of the 6 encoding-sequence slots began. Index aligns with `slot_index_in_seq` (0..5). Slots with no event in this trial remain null. Stamped on every `*_encoding` row. For T-only / I+T M-slots the visible event is the tone, but the timestamp still marks the slot's local start (the planned time at which the tone was handed to the audio clock; the measured scheduling is in `slot_tone_events`).

slot_offsets_ts_ms.description: Per-slot OFFSET timestamps (rounded ms) on the same performance.now() scale as `slot_onsets_ts_ms`; index aligns with `slot_index_in_seq` (0..5); placeholders (dummies) included. Dots, stars and placeholders: the animation-frame time of the first frame without the element (source 'frame'), or the time of the removal call ('removal_call') if no frame arrived before the node ended. Tones: the PLANNED onset plus the nominal tone duration (`slot_tone_events[].nominal_duration_ms`; source 'scheduled': scheduled, not measured). Null if the slot's event never happened (aborted trial) or was still running when the node was cut short (source 'aborted'). Stamped on every `*_encoding` row.

slot_offset_sources.description: How each entry of `slot_offsets_ts_ms` was obtained: 'frame', 'removal_call', 'scheduled' (tones: not measured) or 'aborted' (event cut short: offset is null). Null if there is no offset. Same indexing as `slot_offsets_ts_ms`. The onset of a tone in `slot_onsets_ts_ms` is likewise scheduled (planned), not measured.

slot_planned_onsets_ts_ms.description: Planned onset of each slot on the performance.now() scale (the run origin t0 taken in the encoding node plus the planned time: 1500 ms pre-encoding pad, 1500 ms per memory slot, 3500 ms per star slot). Filled for all six slots as soon as the node starts, so it is complete even in an aborted trial. `slot_onsets_ts_ms - slot_planned_onsets_ts_ms` is the onset error (0 for tones, whose recorded onset is the planned one).

slot_planned_offsets_ts_ms.description: Planned offset of each slot on the same scale: planned onset plus 1000 ms (dot or placeholder in a memory slot), 3000 ms (star or placeholder in a star slot) or 350 ms (tone). The 500 ms after a dot or star and the remaining 1150 ms after a tone are the planned silence before the next slot.

slot_event_kinds.description: What each of the six slots shows, by slot (0..5): 'dot', 'tone', 'star', or 'dummy' (an invisible placeholder that only equalises trial length: nothing is presented). Dummies are not perceptible; the silence between perceptible events includes their intervals.

slot_audio_context_times_ms.description: Web Audio `AudioContext.currentTime` converted to ms (`× 1000`, rounded) at the moment each M-slot tone was scheduled. Length 6, with `null` entries for non-tone slots (S-slots and any slots not in this trial). Stamped on `t_only_encoding` and `i_t_encoding` rows only. The audio clock has its own time origin (separate from `performance.now()`), so use deltas within this array — not subtractions against `slot_onsets_ts_ms`.

retention_onset_ts_ms.description: performance.now() timestamp (rounded ms) at which the retention frame mounted. Stamped on `d_only_retention`, `t_only_retention`, `i_d_retention`, `i_t_retention` rows. The retention window is `RETENTION_MS` long (config.memory.retention_interval_ms = 2000), so `retention_onset_ts_ms + 2000` ≈ first probe onset.

probe_onset_ts_ms.description: performance.now() timestamp (rounded ms) at the moment the probe stimulus was added on top of the mounted frame (white dot for D-only / I+D, tone scheduled for T-only / I+T). Stamped on every `*_probe` row. `response_rt_ms` on the same row is measured relative to this onset, so absolute response time = `probe_onset_ts_ms + response_rt_ms`.

star_onset_ts_ms.description: performance.now() timestamp (rounded ms) at which a star stimulus rendered inside an imagery encoding sequence. Stamped on `i_only_star`, `i_d_star`, `i_t_star` aux rows. Combined with the surrounding `slot_onsets_ts_ms` array on the encoding row, this lets analysts recover the exact inter-star spacing each participant experienced.

audio_context_time_at_onset_ms.description: Web Audio `AudioContext.currentTime × 1000` (rounded ms) at the moment the probe tone was scheduled. Stamped on `t_only_probe` and `i_t_probe` rows. The audio clock has its own time origin separate from `performance.now()`.

iti_onset_ts_ms.description: performance.now() timestamp (rounded ms) at which the post-trial inter-trial-interval frame mounted. Stamped on every `<condition>_iti` row. The ITI is fixed at 800 ms by default (the `itiNode` `ms` parameter), so `iti_onset_ts_ms + 800` is about the next trial's preamble onset.

rest_started_ts_ms.description: performance.now() timestamp (rounded ms) at which a rest screen rendered. Stamped on `rest` rows (inter-block and intra-block). `rest_ended_ts_ms - rest_started_ts_ms` is the realised rest length: `config.blocks.rest_duration_s` (30 s) for an intra-block rest, and up to `config.blocks.inter_block_rest_max_s` (600 s) for the inter-block rest, which the participant may end early with both arrow keys.

rest_ended_ts_ms.description: performance.now() timestamp (rounded ms) at which the rest countdown reached zero (or the rest was ended early) and the node finished. Stamped on `rest` rows. Use with `rest_started_ts_ms` to compute the realised rest length.

rest_planned_s.description: Planned rest length in seconds: 600 (`config.blocks.inter_block_rest_max_s`, a maximum) on the inter-block rest row (`block_label = inter_block`), 30 (`config.blocks.rest_duration_s`) on the intra-block rest rows. Stamped on every `rest` row.

rest_actual_ms.description: Realised rest length in ms, from the moment the rest screen rendered to the moment it ended (timer end, or both arrow keys on the inter-block rest). Stamped on every `rest` row. Before 2026-11-13 the inter-block rest was a forced 30 s, and the 2026-11-13 first version of this change was 120 s ended with Space; see pre-reg/AMENDMENT-inter-block-rest.md.

rest_skipped.description: True if the participant ended the (inter-block) rest early by pressing both arrow keys together (possible only after the first 2 s). Always false on intra-block rests, which cannot be ended early. Stamped on every `rest` row.

rest_timed_out.description: True on the inter-block `rest` row if the full `rest_planned_s` ran out without the participant pressing both arrow keys; the session then ends with `exit_reason = inter_block_rest_timeout` and the participant is sent back to Prolific with the screen-out completion code. False otherwise (always false on intra-block rests). Stamped on every `rest` row.

space_enabled_after_ms.description: `main_a_intro` row only. Time in ms from the start of the screen until Space was enabled (Space is inactive until the voiceover has finished). null if Space was enabled at once (voice off or no recording).

narration_finished.description: `main_a_intro` row only. True if Space was enabled because the recording played to its end.

gate_reason.description: `main_a_intro` row only. Why Space was enabled: the recording ended (`narration_end`), the participant's voice toggle was off (`voice_off`), the safety timeout ran out (`timeout`), or there was no audio to wait for (`no_audio`: recording missing, failed to load, or playback blocked by the browser). `locked_exit` = the screen was left (experimenter keys U/R or the debug N N skip) while Space was still locked.

condition.description: Experimental condition of the trial. Stamped on every row of a trial (gate, cue, imagination, encoding, retention, probe, star, ITI, pattern phase).

trial_uid.description: Trial identifier, unique within a session for main trials (block, presentation index, condition), e.g. main_a-007-i_d. Practice identifiers are unique within a practice pass; a repeated practice pass reuses them (the exporter numbers the passes in `attempt`).

presentation_index.description: Order of the trial over the whole main task, 1-120 across main_a and main_b. Null in practice.

block_position.description: RAW value, 0-based: position of the trial inside its block, in presentation order. The exported tables (tidy 1.2.0) write it 1-based.

pool_index.description: Same RAW value as `trial_index_in_block` (0-based index in the condition's 24-trial pool; exported 1-based); stamped under an unambiguous name.

pattern_reminder.description: True when this trial carries the 4 s pattern reminder (a `pattern_phase` row exists for it). Planned from the trial-type sequence by src/scheduler/pattern-reminders.js; only imagery-bearing trials (i_only, i_d, i_t) can carry it.

trials_since_pattern_reminder.description: Imagery-bearing trials: number of trials since the last pattern reminder in the block (0 on a reminded trial; at most pattern_phase_frequency_trials + 1). Null on memory-only trials (d_only, t_only).

background_shade.description: Page background of the trial. Exactly 12 white and 12 gray per condition, 6 and 6 in each main block.

sequence.description: Six-slot sequence of the trial, M = memory-item slot, S = star slot. One of 14 sequences (run length at most 2, three of each letter).

trial_spec.description: Plan of the whole trial as drawn by the scheduler, stamped on the encoding row: condition, rotation_deg (imagery conditions, else null), display_rotation_deg (d_only, else null), sequence, memory_items [{slot, encoding_position, cell, pattern_label}], stars [{slot, probe_position, cell, pattern_label}], dummies [{slot, cell}] (placeholders; never visible) and probes [{probe_position, encoding_position, type, cell, is_target, pattern_label}]. Slots, probe_position and encoding_position are RAW 0-based values (the exported tables add 1). The exporter reads it so that a star or probe row that was not recorded can still be listed.

probe_frame_rotation_deg.description: Rotation of the frame the recognition probe was drawn in (0 = upright grid).

probe_x_mm.description: Horizontal position of the probe cell centre on the screen, mm, origin at fixation, x right, after `probe_frame_rotation_deg`.

probe_y_mm.description: Vertical position of the probe cell centre on the screen, mm, origin at fixation, y down.

probe_radius_mm.description: Distance of the probe cell centre from fixation, mm (does not depend on rotation).

star_frame_rotation_deg.description: Rotation of the grid the star was drawn in (the trial rotation).

star_x_mm.description: Horizontal screen position of the star centre, mm, origin at fixation, x right.

star_y_mm.description: Vertical screen position of the star centre, mm, origin at fixation, y down.

star_radius_mm.description: Distance of the star cell centre from fixation, mm.

session_id.description: Prolific session id, or a locally generated `LOCAL_…` id when the URL carried no SESSION_ID (see `session_id_source`).

session_id_source.description: `session_info`: where `session_id` came from. `prolific` = the SESSION_ID URL parameter; `local_fallback` = generated in the browser because the parameter was missing (the session is then also `is_preview`).

prng_algorithm.description: Name of the generator behind the schedule.

prng_seed_string.description: Seed string: PROLIFIC_PID|STUDY_ID|SESSION_ID (a random preview string when the URL has no Prolific parameters). The whole schedule can be rebuilt from it.

grid_cells_per_side.description: Cells per side of the square grid (5).

cell_size_mm.description: Side of one grid cell, mm.

dot_diameter_mm.description: Diameter of a memory dot, mm.

star_size_mm.description: Bounding diameter of a star, mm.

open_square_size_mm.description: Side of a placeholder square, mm (placeholders are mounted but not shown).

on_pattern_cells.description: The 12 on-pattern cells (pattern cells without the centre).

rotation_min_deg.description: Lower end of the rotation range.

rotation_max_deg.description: Upper end of the rotation range.

rotation_strata.description: Angle strata used to draw rotations.

cell_table.description: All 25 cells: row, column, upright-grid position (mm from fixation), distance from fixation and on / off / centre label.

run_id.description: Id of the page load that wrote the row (8 characters). A reload or a second visit from the same browser gets a new id; uploads send the rows of one run, and the exporter separates runs.

wall_ms.description: Date.now() when the row was written (trial rows: when the trial finished). Pairs with `clock_anchor` to place `performance.now()` stamps in calendar time.

clock_anchor.description: One reading of every clock at the same moment, written on `session_start` and `session_info`: `perf_now_ms` (performance.now()), `time_origin_ms` (performance.timeOrigin), `date_now_ms` (Date.now()), `iso`, `jspsych_start_ms` (start of the jsPsych timeline, null before it).

prior_rows.description: `session_start`: rows left in this browser by earlier runs.

prior_rows_discarded.description: `session_start`: how many of those rows were removed from this browser because they belonged to an abandoned earlier attempt (a restart begins the study again, so such rows are of no use).

prior_run_ids_discarded.description: `session_start`: run ids of the abandoned earlier attempts whose rows were removed.

prior_run_ids_kept.description: `session_start`: run ids of earlier runs that were kept because they had finished (reached the end of the task, the end-of-session upload or the redirect, or were ended by a screen-out check); their rows stay in the browser for the recovery page.

prior_discard_error.description: `session_start`: error message if clearing the abandoned earlier attempt failed (the session starts anyway), else null.

is_reload.description: `session_start`: true if the page load was a reload.

started_at_iso.description: ISO time at which the session object was created (page load).

plugin_version.description: jsPsych built-in: version of the plugin that ran the trial.

value.description: Return value of a call-function node (calibration, checks, summaries): an object whose fields depend on the phase.

user_gain.description: Participant's playback gain (0-1) in force when the trial finished.

hidden_nav_step.description: Step id the row belongs to in the development navigation.

stimulus.description: jsPsych built-in: markup shown on the trial, kept on instruction and form rows.

consent_version.description: `consent`: label of the consent form shown.

display_colour_locked.description: True if the display-colour lock was applied.

cal_pass.description: `screen_calibration`: which of the two settings of the attempt this was (1 or 2).

cal_start_kind.description: `screen_calibration`: whether the slider started low or high.

cal_start_px.description: `screen_calibration`: starting width of the card rectangle, px.

cal_t_first_input_ms.description: `screen_calibration`: time of the first slider input, ms from the start of the pass.

cal_t_last_input_ms.description: `screen_calibration`: time of the last slider input, ms from the start of the pass.

cal_dwell_ms.description: `screen_calibration`: time spent on the pass, ms.

cal_trace.description: `screen_calibration`: slider trace as [time ms, width px] pairs.

px_per_mm_in_bounds.description: True if the calibrated px per mm lies in the plausible range.

px_per_mm_min.description: Lower limit of the plausible px per mm.

px_per_mm_max.description: Upper limit of the plausible px per mm.

snap_iso.description: Display snapshot: ISO time of the reading.

screen_w.description: Display snapshot: screen width, CSS px.

screen_h.description: Display snapshot: screen height, CSS px.

avail_w.description: Display snapshot: available screen width, CSS px.

avail_h.description: Display snapshot: available screen height, CSS px.

color_depth.description: Display snapshot: screen colour depth, bits.

inner_w.description: Display snapshot: window inner width, CSS px.

inner_h.description: Display snapshot: window inner height, CSS px.

outer_w.description: Display snapshot: window outer width, CSS px.

outer_h.description: Display snapshot: window outer height, CSS px.

zoom_proxy_outer_inner.description: Display snapshot: outer width divided by inner width (a zoom proxy).

is_fullscreen.description: Display snapshot: the page is fullscreen.

platform.description: Display snapshot: platform reported by the browser.

ua_mobile.description: Display snapshot: the browser reports a mobile device.

kind.description: Event rows (`visibility_event`, `display_guard_event`): kind of event. `runtime_error`: `error` or `unhandledrejection`.

message.description: `runtime_error`, `runtime_error_fatal`: error message cut to 300 characters; no stack, URL or page text.

source.description: `runtime_error`: file name and line:column of the source, without host or path.

trial_phase.description: `runtime_error`: `phase` of the trial that was running when the error happened, if known.

stage.description: `runtime_error_fatal`: where the session failed (a storage failure cannot be written).

audio_state.description: `audio_state_change`: the AudioContext state the browser switched to (running, suspended, interrupted, closed).

redirect_after_failed_upload.description: `completion_redirect`: the participant went to Prolific after the end-of-session upload had failed, using the Continue button on the failure screen.

upload_attempt.description: `upload_retry_result`: number of the upload attempt made on the failure screen after the end-of-session upload failed (1 = first retry).

after_failure.description: `upload_retry_result`: always true; the attempt came after the end-of-session upload had failed.

retry_trigger.description: `upload_retry_result`: what started the attempt: the participant pressing 'Try sending my answers again', or the one last attempt made when 'Continue to Prolific' was pressed.

previous_status.description: `upload_retry_result`: the status the end-of-session upload row (`upload_session_end`) had recorded before this attempt.

download_filename.description: `upload_session_end`: name of the data file saved to the device after a failed upload (contains a random token, no Prolific id).

failed_buckets.description: `upload_session_end`: ids of the buckets that could not be sent (every bucket is tried).

ts.description: Event rows and `unload_attempt` / `back_pressed`: performance.now() when the event happened.

iso.description: Event rows: ISO time of the event.

guard_flags.description: Display-guard events (comma-separated kinds) that happened since the previous trial finished; the trial is affected. Absent when there were none.

t_first_slider_input_ms.description: `tone_audibility_and_comfort`: time of the first slider input, ms from the start of the trial.

applied_peak_dbfs.description: `tone_audibility_and_comfort`: peak level of an uncompensated tone at the final slider position, dBFS.

audio_context.description: State of the audio context when the row was written: `sample_rate_hz`, `state`, `base_latency_ms` (processing delay of the context) and `output_latency_ms` (delay to the audio device), each as reported by the browser.

frame_sd_ms.description: `timing_probe`: standard deviation of the frame interval, ms.

frame_p95_ms.description: `timing_probe`: 95th percentile of the frame interval, ms.

frame_dropped_frac.description: `timing_probe`: share of frames that took more than 1.5 median intervals.

timeout_overshoot_median_ms.description: `timing_probe`: median lateness of a 0 ms timer, ms.

page_hidden_during_probe.description: `timing_probe`: the page was hidden during the probe.

practice_iteration.description: Pass through the practice block (1 or 2). On `practice_iteration_start`, `practice_feedback` and every practice trial row, so a repeated pass can be told apart.

final_practice_correct.description: `practice_disqualification`: correct responses in the last pass.

view_history.description: jsPsych built-in (instruction pages): page index and viewing time of each page view.

demo_advanced_via_space.description: Demo rows: the demo was ended with Space.

demo_arrow_presses.description: Demo rows: how many times the participant pressed an arrow key while the 'Just watch and listen' banner was on screen (the demo presses the keys itself; each press made the banner jiggle). Key repeats are not counted.

gate_show_arrow.description: Trial-start gate: the trial is an imagery trial (the arrow follows the gate).

gate_rotation_deg.description: Trial-start gate: rotation shown by the arrow, null if none.

gate_trial_type.description: Trial-start gate: condition label shown to the participant.

notice_task.description: `practice_buttons_notice`: the single task whose first practice trial the notice followed (the zoomed response buttons and the message that they are not shown in the main trials).

gate_prominent.description: Trial-start gate: the instruction was shown as the centred, coloured-border box (the first practice trial of each task, right after its demonstration) instead of the small pill at the bottom.

gate_passed_at_ms.description: Trial-start gate: ms from gate onset to the moment both arrow keys were down.

gate_post_delay_ms.description: Trial-start gate: delay between the key press and the end of the gate, ms.

main_trial_number_overall.description: Trial-start gate: number of the trial over the main task, shown to the participant.

main_trial_total.description: Trial-start gate: number of main-task trials.

main_trial_type.description: Trial-start gate: condition of the trial.

planned_total_ms.description: Encoding row: planned length of the encoding node, ms.

key_log.description: Encoding row: every arrow key press as [R or L, ms after `key_log_t0_ms`], at most 80 entries (see `key_log_overflow`).

key_log_t0_ms.description: Encoding row: performance.now() at the start of the encoding schedule, the origin of `key_log`.

key_log_overflow.description: Encoding row: more key presses than `key_log` holds.

memory_items.description: Encoding row: the memory items as shown, with slot, cell, encoding position, pattern label and, for tones, bank index and frequency.

dummies.description: Encoding row: placeholder cells by slot.

stars.description: Encoding row: star cells by slot.

keys_outside_window.description: Encoding row: arrow key presses while no star window was open.

slot_positions_mm.description: Encoding row: for each slot, what it showed (`kind`: dot, dummy, star or tone), the cell and its position `x_mm`, `y_mm` in the frame it was drawn in (origin at fixation, y down). A tone has no visual position; its entry holds the upright position of its paired cell.

slot_tone_events.description: Encoding row: one entry per tone: slot, cell, tone_index, `planned_ts_ms`, `perf_at_schedule_ms` and `ac_time_at_schedule_ms` (both clocks when the tone was scheduled), `when_ms` (scheduled start on the audio clock), `scheduled_onset_perf_ms` (time on the performance.now() scale at which the device is expected to emit the tone, from the context's output timestamp, so it includes the output delay; null if the browser gives no clock pairing), `nominal_duration_ms` (350) and `scheduled_offset_perf_ms` (scheduled onset plus nominal duration; null if there is no scheduled onset), `late` and `late_ms` (scheduling came after the planned onset, and by how much), `error` (message if playing failed, else null).

tone_error.description: True if a tone of the trial could not be played (encoding row: any tone; probe row: the probe tone). Details in `slot_tone_events[].error` or `tone_error_message`.

tone_error_message.description: Probe row: message of the error when the probe tone could not be played.

rotation_start_ts_ms.description: Encoding row: performance.now() at the frame in which the rotation animation was started; null if the trial has no rotation.

audio_output_latency_ms.description: Sum of the audio context's output latency and base latency, ms (encoding rows of all conditions; probe rows of tone conditions). The two parts are in `audio_context`.

audio_perf_at_onset_ms.description: Tone probe row: performance.now() when the probe tone was handed to the audio context.

early_keypresses.description: Probe and star rows: arrow key presses before the stimulus onset.

late_keypresses.description: Probe and star rows: arrow key presses after the response window closed.

extra_keypresses.description: Probe and star rows: arrow key presses after the first valid response.

duration_ms.description: Planned duration of a pattern phase, arrow cue or imagination period, ms.

imagination_onset_ts_ms.description: performance.now() timestamp (rounded ms) at which the imagination period began.

pattern_onset_ts_ms.description: performance.now() timestamp (rounded ms) at which the pattern reminder was shown. Stamped on `pattern_phase` rows.

frame_rotation_deg.description: Rotation of the grid while the node was on screen (0 = upright). On retention, probe, ITI, arrow-cue and imagination rows; `rotation_deg` on the arrow-cue and imagination rows is the angle to imagine, and the frame is upright there.

star_onset_lag_ms.description: Star row: star onset minus its planned onset, ms.

window_closed_ts_ms.description: Star row: performance.now() when the response window closed.

displayed.description: Star row: the star was shown.

truncated.description: Star row: the node ended before the window finished, or the star was never shown.

is_preview.description: `session_info`: the URL carried no Prolific parameters.

debug_mode.description: `session_info` and upload envelope: true when the experimenter debug tools (console trace, secret grid reveal; see DEBUGGING.md) were active in this session. Only possible on a pilot, dev or localhost session with `debug=1` in the URL. Exclude such sessions from analysis.

debug_reveal_on.description: `debug_reveal`: true when the hidden grid and pattern were switched on, false when switched off.

debug_node_phase.description: `debug_reveal`: `phase` of the trial node that was running when the reveal was toggled.

resume_latency_ms.description: `rest_resume_gate`: time to press both keys, ms.

status.description: `upload_session_end`: result of the end-of-session upload (uploaded, partial, no_endpoint, nothing_to_upload, timed_out, unknown). `upload_retry_result`: result of that retry attempt (the same values, or error). The LATEST of these rows is the final upload status.

downloadFallback.description: `upload_session_end`: the data were also offered as a download.

storage_write_failures.description: `upload_session_end`: rows that could not be written to browser storage.

storage_last_error.description: `upload_session_end`: message of the last storage failure.

storage_last_failure_at.description: `upload_session_end`: ISO time of the last storage failure.

build_commit.description: `session_info`: commit the build was made from ('dev' when unbuilt or git was not available).

build_time.description: `session_info`: time the build was made ('dev' when unbuilt).

consent_text_sha256.description: `session_info`: SHA-256 of the consent form markup shown.

instruction_deck_sha256.description: `session_info`: SHA-256 of the text of each instruction deck (overview, practice_readiness, d_only, t_only, i_only, i_d, i_t) and of the demo narration.

strategy_items_sha256.description: `session_info`: SHA-256 of the strategy questionnaire scale, sections and items.

tone_params.description: `session_info`: the tone bank as played: `peak_amplitude` (before gain), `duration_ms`, `cosine_ramp_ms` and `bank`, one entry per tone with index, frequency, gain compensation in dB, pattern label and paired cell.

_phase_field_documentation_only_.description: This document intentionally does not enumerate per-phase required-field constraints (e.g. via `oneOf` over `phase`-discriminated branches). Reason: per-phase variation is large (50+ phase tags), the constraints would duplicate the runtime contracts already locked by unit tests, and a stricter schema would make minor field additions during pilot painful for marginal validation gain. Analysts who want stricter per-phase shapes should write Pandera / Pydantic schemas downstream from this raw-row schema.
